key_insight: Flow-dependent LSQ LES filter-widths can transmit floating-point perturbations with little attenuation, so mesh-metric noise may affect the SGS model and downstream flow physics.
engineering_relevance: For heterogeneous CPU/GPU LES, the filter-width formulation should be numerically robust because small arithmetic differences can alter predictions in sensitive transitional flows.
method: Analyzed how floating-point disturbances enter through mesh metrics in the LSQ filter-width operator
Introduced a scalar max–min compression of directional mesh scales
Added bounded modulation from the resolved velocity gradient to preserve flow dependence while reducing sensitivity
evidence_signal: Evaluated on heterogeneous CPU and GPU runs for cylinder flow at Re=3900 and Taylor–Green vortex at Re=1600, showing strong transmission in the cylinder case but no comparable macroscopic effect on orthogonal Taylor–Green grids.
watch_item: The mitigation changes the original LSQ construction, so implementation must balance robustness against preserving physically meaningful flow dependence.
paper_title: On the transmission of floating-point perturbations in flow-dependent filter-width formulations in Large-Eddy Simulation
